lots.guide_summary: Range from close entries only: A$77 to A$731, both SOLD (no UNSOLD or ASKING same-item entries). The A$731 is a 2014 US sale of a cherub-and-two-lions chariot centrepiece, outside the 24-month window; the only recent one is a different-model Amphora lion-chariot group at US$50 (A$77). Gowans category guides (single or damaged bisque figures) sold for $10 to $60 hammer, and a repaired Royal Dux lion passed in. Rate 1 USD = 1.54 AUD. No same-model sale was found. Web search was capped this session, so no dealer asking prices were gathered.
lots.working: No SOLD entry is the same item (same model, lady leading two lions with a chariot bowl) in the last 24 months, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0 under the rules. For context only: the recent close sale (A$77) / 1.198 = A$64, which would round down to $60 if it counted. Gowans premium 19.8%, all-in = hammer x 1.198.
lots.confidence_reason: Single front photo only; no maker's mark read (the underside is not shown); no same-model sale; the close comparables differ in model or are 12 years old; web search was capped.
lots.dropped_entries: None of the researcher's five Gowans entries were dropped: all five were re-confirmed in the API with the price, date and bid count stated. All are re-labelled as category guide only. The PAIR OF WOODLAND SURPRISES box ($25, lot 392527) is kept off the sold list as too unlike this item to be useful (a mixed box of small modern figures).
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. Woman in pink and lilac gown leading two maned lions, attached to a rococo C-scroll chariot bowl with a pink and green gilt wheel, on a scroll-footed base with a cartouche. Matte bisque-type body with pastel and gilt wash, typical of Austrian or Bohemian (Turn-Teplitz or Royal Dux-type) export wares of c1900-1920. Nothing visibly broken from the front, but the woman's hands, the lion tails and the bowl rim tips could not be checked at this resolution. There is a Gowans tag tied around the figure's neck. No mark visible.
lots.condition: Appears intact from the front in one photo; not verified. Typical risks: chips or restoration to fingers, lion tails and ears, the chariot scroll tips and the base feet; gilt wear.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please check the underside for a maker's mark or impressed numbers (for example Royal Dux pink triangle, Amphora or Turn-Teplitz marks) and confirm the overall length, and check the woman's hands, the lion tails and ears, the chariot scroll tips and the base feet for chips, cracks or glued repairs.
